MeteoGalicia validation codes

Source: R/utils-quality.R
meteogal_qc_codes.Rd

Table of the validation codes (lnCodigoValidacion) that MeteoGalicia attaches to every measurement in its daily and hourly JSON services, together with the way these codes are treated by the package.

meteogal_qc_codes()

Value

A data.frame with columns code, description, default (TRUE when admitted by the default quality = c(1, 5)) and usable (FALSE for codes that can never be admitted).

Details

Each measurement <variable> can be accompanied by an integer column qc_<variable>. The quality argument of meteogal2df(), meteogal2fdata() and meteogal2lfdata() specifies which codes are admitted. Values with other codes are set to NA in the returned object, while the original codes are retained.

Codes 3 (erroneous) and 9 (not recorded) are never used. A missing validation code means that its status is unknown; such observations are retained and counted as having unknown validation status.

The sentinel value -9999, documented by MeteoGalicia as representing no data, is always treated as missing.

References

MeteoGalicia. Daily meteorological-station data (JSON): https://www.meteogalicia.gal/datosred/infoweb/meteo/docs/rss/JSON_EstacionsDiarios_es.pdf.

MeteoGalicia. Historical hourly station data (JSON), same validation codes: https://www.meteogalicia.gal/datosred/infoweb/meteo/docs/rss/JSON_EstacionHorariosHistoricos_es.pdf.

MeteoGalicia. Current station state (JSON), -9999 = no data: https://www.meteogalicia.gal/datosred/infoweb/meteo/docs/rss/JSON_estado_actual_es.pdf.

Examples

meteogal_qc_codes()
#>   code        description default usable
#> 1    0      Not validated   FALSE   TRUE
#> 2    1     Valid original    TRUE   TRUE
#> 3    2            Suspect   FALSE   TRUE
#> 4    3          Erroneous   FALSE  FALSE
#> 5    5 Valid interpolated    TRUE   TRUE
#> 6    9       Not recorded   FALSE  FALSE
